mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a robust demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as lower borrowing costs stimulate economic activity and investment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market is a leading indicator of broader economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST decreases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
